prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added `heading_offset` (0–5, default 0; any other value, including bools and floats, raises ValueError) to `markdown.Markdown` and `markdown.markdown`. It works through a new built-in tree processor, `HeadingOffsetTreeprocessor` (priority 9), so it runs after every heading is built, md_in_html ones included, and before `toc` (priority 5). That way toc's tokens and `toc_depth` see the shifted levels, which are capped at h6. Raw HTML headings without `markdown="1"` stay as written. The command line gets `--heading-offset N` and rejects values outside 0–5 with a usage error. The full suite passes (`OK`, 112 skipped, the same skip count as before the change). I also added docs and a changelog entry under a new `[unreleased]` section. In the CLI docs, the help listing now also shows the existing `-n/--no_lazy_ol` line so it matches the real `--help` output.
